hero.headline: Republicans demand detailed answers before approving Iran military funding
hero.body:
Republicans in Congress are withholding support for a funding request to finance ongoing military operations in Iran, saying they want clearer information from the Pentagon about the scope, objectives, and total cost of the campaign before backing the measure in an election year.

The military operation, which has now passed its 100-day mark, has cost roughly $29 billion so far. Republican lawmakers are seeking more detailed projections and strategic clarity from defense officials before committing to additional funding. The hesitation reflects concerns about committing taxpayer dollars to an extended military engagement without a clear endpoint or comprehensive plan.

The request for more information comes as the administration seeks congressional approval for continued funding of the operation. Republicans face political pressure in what is described as a difficult election year, with voters likely to scrutinize large-scale military spending abroad. The Pentagon has not yet provided the level of detail lawmakers say they need to justify supporting the request to constituents.

The funding debate arrives at a moment when the administration's Iran strategy faces broader questions. President Trump initially said the operation would last four to five weeks, but it has now extended well beyond that timeframe. The discrepancy between initial projections and the current reality has added to congressional skepticism about committing additional resources without more concrete assurances.

The standoff highlights tension between the executive and legislative branches over war powers and spending authority. Republicans control the House, giving them significant leverage over any funding package. Without their support, the administration may struggle to secure the resources it says are necessary to continue operations at their current pace.

cards.headline: Iran war passes 100 days as Trump negotiation efforts face setbacks
cards.teaser: The military operation has far exceeded the president's initial timeline of four to five weeks.
cards.body:
President Trump's goal of quickly ending the Iran war has stalled as the conflict surpassed 100 days. Trump initially projected the operation would last four to five weeks, but active fighting continues without resolution.

The extended timeline undermines Trump's reputation as a dealmaker. A recent Iranian attack that downed a U.S. Army Apache helicopter prompted Trump to say the country "must" respond, complicating his earlier optimistic statements about negotiations. Meanwhile, gas prices have surged to $4.16 per gallon nationally—about $1 higher than last year—straining household budgets as the conflict drags on.

cards.headline: Markets Fall as Investors Await Inflation Data and Monitor Middle East Tensions
cards.body:
Stock markets declined globally as investors braced for inflation data while monitoring escalating tensions in the Middle East. The Strait of Hormuz remained closed following a weekend of military exchanges between Iran and the United States, disrupting oil markets and rattling investor confidence.

Britain's FTSE 100 fell 58.5 points, or 0.55%, to close at 10,609 points, retreating from a six-week high reached Friday. European markets also retreated, with the Stoxx 600 dropping around 0.9% in late trading. Germany's DAX and France's CAC 40 each lost approximately 1%, while Italy's FTSE MIB fell 1.2%.

The oil market showed volatility, with prices rising 5.5% to reach $95.20 a barrel after reversing half of Friday's losses. However, the Strait of Hormuz closure kept energy markets on edge. UK month-ahead gas prices climbed 3% to around 100 pence per therm.

In the United States, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both fell, with the Nasdaq dropping 0.55% to 24,334 points. The decline came after the Nasdaq had posted 13 consecutive daily gains on Friday, the longest winning streak since early 1992. Travel stocks experienced particular weakness, with Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings falling 4%.

The Middle East situation created fresh uncertainty after a chaotic weekend. Though Iran and the United States had signaled Friday that the strait had reopened, it remained closed Monday. Ships attempting to navigate the waterway either turned back after coming under fire or tested channels without passing through completely. The U.S. also seized an Iranian vessel in the Gulf of Oman.

The ceasefire between the two nations is set to expire mid-week, with expectations for peace talks still uncertain. President Trump said extending a two-week ceasefire was "highly unlikely" unless a deal materialized, stating he would not be rushed into an agreement.

Anthony Willis, senior economist at Columbia Threadneedle Investments, noted that developments over the weekend had muddied the situation. He pointed to the limited ship movement through the strait and escalatory rhetoric from both sides, including U.S. threats against Iranian infrastructure and Iranian pushback on nuclear concessions.

Joe Mazzola, head trading and derivatives strategist at Charles Schwab, described the shift from Friday's optimism as "the Monday blues after Middle East anxiety re-ignited over the weekend."

The consumer price index report looms as investors assess whether the data will clarify the Federal Reserve's interest rate path or add to market uncertainty. The combination of inflation concerns, geopolitical instability, and ongoing technology stock pressures has left global markets sensitive to developments on multiple fronts. A lasting resolution to Middle East tensions and clarity on inflation remain critical factors for market direction in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: Artificial Intelligence Threatens Middle-Class Back-Office Jobs
cards.teaser: AI technology is spreading beyond coding roles to target millions of positions in human resources, billing, and payroll, with women holding most of the affected jobs.
cards.body:
The expansion of artificial intelligence into back-office operations poses risks to millions of middle-class jobs that have traditionally been considered stable. Positions in human resources, billing, and payroll are increasingly vulnerable to automation as AI systems become more capable of handling routine administrative tasks. Women hold the majority of these roles, making the potential displacement particularly significant for gender equity in the workforce.

The shift represents a broader transformation than the initial focus on how AI might affect software developers and other technical positions. Back-office functions have long provided steady employment for college-educated workers, but advances in AI are making it possible for companies to automate many of these tasks. The development raises questions about how workers in these fields will adapt and what support systems might be needed to help them transition to other roles.

cards.headline: SpaceX Prepares for Stock Market Debut
cards.teaser: The space company is moving toward its initial public offering, with demand approaching four times oversubscribed according to sources familiar with the matter.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing to go public in what would be one of the most anticipated stock market debuts in recent years. The company's IPO has generated significant interest from institutional investors, with sources indicating that demand has reached nearly four times the available shares. The offering will test investor appetite for high-profile technology companies at a time when the sector has faced headwinds.

The IPO comes as SpaceX continues to develop its Starship program, which aims to enable missions to Mars. Analysts have debated whether the proposed $135-per-share valuation is justified, with some questioning whether the offering will follow the pattern of other mega-IPOs that have struggled after their debuts. The public listing will have implications for founder Elon Musk, everyday investors seeking exposure to the space industry, and investment banks managing the offering.

cards.headline: NASA names crew for Artemis III moon landing mission
cards.body:
NASA announced the four astronauts selected for the Artemis III mission on Tuesday, marking a significant step toward returning humans to the lunar surface. The crew will conduct a two-week orbital test flight in 2027 before the planned first crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV in 2028.

The crew consists of three American astronauts and one European. Randy Bresnik, a Marine colonel and former International Space Station commander, will serve as mission commander. Frank Rubio, an Army Black Hawk helicopter pilot and flight surgeon, holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a NASA astronaut at 371 days. Andre Douglas, a systems engineer and Coast Guard reserve officer, will round out the NASA contingent. Luca Parmitano, an Italian astronaut with the European Space Agency, will pilot the mission.

Unlike the Artemis II mission that circled the moon in April, Artemis III will remain in lower Earth orbit. The crew will test docking procedures and life support systems with lunar landers developed by Blue Origin and SpaceX. These tests will determine which lander system performs best ahead of the actual moon landing on Artemis IV.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman described the effort as "Earth's first starfleet" during the announcement in Houston. He emphasized the scale of the undertaking, noting the numerous spacecraft that will operate simultaneously in orbit, including vessels from multiple nations and companies.

The Artemis program represents an international collaboration. Parmitano's selection reflects the partnership between NASA and the European Space Agency, which provides service modules for the Orion spacecraft. The mission involves contributions from multiple countries participating in lunar exploration efforts.

The Artemis IV landing in 2028 will mark the first crewed lunar touchdown since Apollo 17 in 1972. NASA plans to land astronauts near the moon's south pole, a region containing water ice in permanently shadowed craters that differs from the equatorial sites visited during the Apollo program.

Blue Origin's lunar lander program faced a setback on May 28 when its New Glenn rocket exploded during a launch pad test in Florida. John Couluris, Blue Origin's senior vice-president of lunar permanence, acknowledged the "significant anomaly" but expressed confidence that the company and launch pad would be ready for next year's flight. Jeremy Parsons, NASA's acting deputy associate administrator for the moon to Mars program, stated that NASA is actively working with Blue Origin to address the incident and ensure mission success.

The Artemis III crew will undergo intensive training for the complex mission. Bresnik brings extensive spaceflight experience from previous shuttle missions and ISS command. Rubio's record spaceflight duration demonstrates his capability for extended missions. Parmitano, a former fighter pilot, survived a dangerous spacesuit malfunction during a 2013 spacewalk from the ISS. Douglas, though new to spaceflight, trained as part of the Artemis II backup crew.

cards.headline: Trump pushes Senate leader Thune on SAVE Act as MAGA base applies pressure
cards.teaser: President Trump's renewed push to oust the Senate parliamentarian and pass voter eligibility legislation is creating tension for the majority leader.
cards.body:
President Trump has intensified efforts to remove the Senate parliamentarian and advance the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act, placing new pressure on Senate Majority Leader John Thune. Thune, who has had an inconsistent relationship with Trump over the years, is becoming a target of criticism from the MAGA base as he navigates the president's demands.

Thune is not up for reelection in the current cycle, but the pressure campaign reflects Trump's willingness to challenge Republican leaders who do not fall in line with his priorities. The push for the SAVE Act and the effort to remove the parliamentarian represent a test of Trump's influence over Senate procedures and leadership.

hero.headline: Pakistan Launches Air Strikes in Afghanistan
hero.teaser: Pakistan conducted air strikes in Afghanistan, ending weeks of relative calm and reigniting tensions along the border between the two countries.
hero.body:
Pakistan launched deadly air strikes in Afghanistan, ending weeks of relative calm in the border region between the two countries. The strikes mark a fresh escalation in tensions.

The restive border area has long been a source of conflict and instability between Pakistan and Afghanistan. The military action follows a period of reduced hostilities that had offered hope for improved relations.

cards.headline: Violence Erupts in Belfast Following Stabbing Attack
cards.teaser: Cars and a bus were set ablaze in Belfast as a stabbing attack sparked street violence that drove families from their homes.
cards.body:
A stabbing incident in Belfast sparked widespread unrest across the city and beyond. The attack, involving a Sudanese man accused of attempting to kill another person, triggered fiery anti-immigration protests that extended into Scotland, where hundreds of demonstrators gathered across the central belt.

During the disorder, vehicles including cars and a bus were set on fire as tensions escalated on Belfast streets. Families were forced to evacuate their homes as the violence spread through affected neighborhoods.

cards.headline: 12 Killed in Johannesburg Mass Shooting
cards.teaser: A mass shooting at an informal settlement in Cleveland, Johannesburg left 12 people dead and nine injured, prompting a manhunt.
cards.body:
Twelve people were killed and nine others wounded in a mass shooting at an informal settlement in Cleveland, Johannesburg, on Tuesday night. Authorities in South Africa have begun a manhunt to find those responsible for the attack.

The incident ranks among the deadliest mass shootings to occur in the area in recent months.

cards.headline: Manslaughter Charges Filed Over Hong Kong Fire That Killed 168
cards.teaser: Authorities laid manslaughter charges over the Wang Fuk Court fire, the deadliest blaze Hong Kong has seen in 70 years.
cards.body:
Hong Kong authorities have filed manslaughter charges related to the Wang Fuk Court fire that claimed 168 lives last year. The blaze stands as the deadliest fire Hong Kong has experienced in seven decades.

The charges represent a major step forward in the investigation into the tragedy, one of the most significant building fires in modern Hong Kong history.

cards.headline: Poland Threatens to Strip Zelensky of Honor Over Military Unit Name
cards.teaser: Poland said it may revoke a state honor from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over the naming of a Ukrainian military unit after controversial World War Two fighters.
cards.body:
Poland is threatening to revoke a state honor awarded to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukraine's decision to name a military unit after controversial World War Two fighters. The naming has created a diplomatic dispute between the two neighboring countries.

The dispute centers on how Poland and Ukraine view the legacy of the historical figures chosen for the unit's name. Poland views the decision as offensive, while Zelensky faces pressure to resolve the disagreement with the Polish government.

cards.headline: Kenyans Protest U.S. Ebola Quarantine Facility Plan
cards.teaser: Hundreds marched in Kenya to oppose a proposed quarantine facility that would be reserved exclusively for American patients.
cards.body:
A man was shot dead by Kenyan police during a protest against a proposed U.S. Ebola quarantine facility in Nanyuki, 120 miles from Nairobi. Patrick Wahome, an organizer of the demonstrations, reported that the victim suffered a fatal gunshot wound to the head.

Kenyans have mobilized against the planned center, which would treat only American patients. Protesters express concerns about cross-border infection risks and insufficient government transparency regarding the facility's operations. The dispute has strained U.S.-Kenya diplomatic relations.

cards.headline: U.S. Immigration Rules Block Some World Cup Visitors
cards.teaser: Fans and participants hoping to attend the World Cup in the United States have faced obstacles due to restrictive immigration policies.
cards.body:
Some fans and participants planning to attend the World Cup in the United States encountered immigration barriers preventing their entry. A World Cup referee from Somalia, Omar Artan, was denied entry to the United States and returned home, where he received a hero's welcome. Artan has vowed to officiate at the 2030 World Cup instead.

The restrictions have drawn criticism from those affected, who view them as overly stringent for a major international sporting event that traditionally welcomes global visitors.

hero.headline: San Francisco immigration court closes as deportation proceedings accelerate nationwide
hero.body:
The Department of Justice shut down the main immigration court in San Francisco last week, eliminating one of the busiest immigration courts in the country that processed thousands of cases annually. The closure removes a court that historically granted asylum applications at one of the highest rates in the nation.

The courthouse on 100 Montgomery Street will cease operations, with a smaller San Francisco facility remaining open. Most court operations will relocate to an immigration court 35 miles away in Concord in the East Bay. The justice department's executive office for immigration review described the closure as "cost effective" in a statement.

The shutdown follows a pattern of significant changes to the immigration court system. Over the past year, the Department of Justice fired 20 of the court's 22 judges. The Trump administration has faced accusations of removing immigration judges in favor of those more aligned with its mass deportation agenda. Similarly, six judges were recently removed from the Concord court, which opened in 2024 as part of an earlier effort to address the growing immigration case backlog.

The San Francisco court's high asylum grant rate had made it a preferred venue for immigrants and their attorneys. The closure will redirect cases to other courts in the region, raising concerns about capacity and delays. As of September 2025, there are 3.75 million pending immigration cases nationwide, according to the executive office for immigration review. In San Francisco alone, there are 120,000 pending cases.

Legal experts question whether the Concord court can handle the inherited caseload. "With so few judges at the Concord court, we're going to see a lot of people waiting years and years and years to have their cases heard," said Milli Atkinson, director of the San Francisco Bar Association's immigrant legal defense program.

Extended delays create practical problems for asylum seekers. Former immigration judge Shira Levine, now deputy legal director for the Immigration Institute of the Bay Area, explained that delays weaken case presentations. "Presenting a lot of oral testimony from themselves and from witnesses," she said. "Over years, testimonial memories can fade."

The court closure and judge removals have created additional complications. Court dates are being rescheduled, and notices are causing confusion among immigrants who may have unstable addresses or limited English proficiency. Missing hearings can trigger Immigration and Customs Enforcement attention.

Atkinson expressed concern that vulnerable people will fall through the system. "If someone gets the wrong date, gets the wrong time, gets the wrong place, doesn't file something exactly correct, the consequences are in some cases where they really do have a serious fear of return, life-threatening."

The closure represents a significant shift in how the immigration court system operates, affecting immigrants throughout the Bay Area seeking legal relief from deportation.

cards.headline: ICE collected data on protesters despite denying database existence
cards.teaser: Immigration enforcement officials acknowledged gathering information on people suspected of potentially unlawful activity, which could include participants in protests.
cards.body:
In a previously unpublicized letter to Congress, the newly-departed head of ICE disclosed that the agency collects data on people suspected of potentially unlawful activity, which could encompass protesters.

This disclosure contradicts ICE's public denials about maintaining a database specifically for tracking protesters. The letter reveals the agency's data collection practices extend beyond what the agency has acknowledged to the public.

cards.headline: Bill Gates to testify before Congress on Jeffrey Epstein relationship
cards.teaser: The Microsoft founder will appear for a closed-door interview with the House Oversight Committee about his connections to the convicted sex offender.
cards.body:
Bill Gates will appear before the House Oversight Committee in a closed-door session to answer questions about his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender who died in federal custody in 2019. The Microsoft co-founder has previously acknowledged meeting with Epstein multiple times, characterizing the meetings as related to philanthropic fundraising efforts.

The testimony is part of the committee's broader investigation into Epstein. A transcript of Gates' interview is expected to be released publicly at a later date.

cards.headline: Texas man sentenced to 35 years for fatal stabbing at high school track meet
cards.teaser: Karmelo Anthony was convicted of murder in the death of Austin Metcalf, a Frisco student who was killed at a track competition.
cards.body:
A jury found Karmelo Anthony guilty of murder in the stabbing death of Austin Metcalf at a Texas track meet. The court sentenced Anthony to 35 years in prison following the verdict.

The stabbing occurred during a track competition involving high school students. Testimony in the trial lasted four days before closing arguments were presented to the jury. Metcalf's father addressed Anthony directly in court following the sentencing.

cards.headline: World Cup tournament opens with expanded 48-team format
cards.teaser: The largest World Cup in history begins this summer with national teams competing across venues in the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
cards.body:
The World Cup is starting with 48 men's national teams, marking the tournament's expansion from the previous 32-team format. The competition represents the biggest World Cup ever held.

The tournament is being hosted jointly by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. This is the first World Cup to feature 48 teams, changing the structure and length of the competition compared to previous editions.

cards.headline: Somali referee denied US entry for World Cup returns home
cards.teaser: Omar Artan, who was barred from entering the United States, arrived in Somalia and pledged to officiate at the 2030 World Cup instead.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, a referee selected to officiate World Cup matches, was denied entry to the United States and returned to Somalia instead. He received a hero's welcome upon arriving home.

Following the incident, Artan announced his intention to officiate at the 2030 World Cup tournament. The situation has drawn attention to visa and entry procedures affecting international sports officials.

cards.headline: China strengthens North Korea ties as Kim pushes nuclear power status
cards.teaser: Xi Jinping remained silent on North Korea's nuclear program as Kim Jong Un worked to establish his country as an irreversible nuclear power.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has reaffirmed diplomatic ties with North Korea while deliberately avoiding the subject of the country's nuclear weapons program. This silence comes as Kim Jong Un seeks international recognition of North Korea's permanent status as a nuclear power.

The renewed relationship between Beijing and Pyongyang complicates U.S. efforts to counter North Korea's nuclear ambitions. China has historically been North Korea's closest ally and primary trading partner, and the two countries have now recommitted to their partnership while sidestepping nuclear tensions entirely.

cards.headline: China's Factory-Gate Inflation Reaches Nearly Four-Year High
cards.teaser: Wholesale prices in China rose at the fastest pace in almost four years, driven by higher input costs from Middle East tensions and demand from the artificial intelligence boom.
cards.body:
China's producer price index climbed to its highest level since 2022, driven by higher commodity costs from the Middle East conflict and strong demand from the artificial intelligence sector. The wholesale inflation surge represents a significant shift in the world's second-largest economy after an extended period of subdued factory-gate prices.

Consumer inflation in China unexpectedly stalled despite rising oil prices. This divergence between wholesale and consumer prices indicates that manufacturers are absorbing increased costs rather than passing them on to shoppers. The producer price gains reflect both external shocks from geopolitical tensions and robust technology sector demand as the AI boom fuels orders for components and materials.

cards.headline: SpaceX Prepares for Stock Market Debut
cards.teaser: The space company is moving toward its initial public offering, with demand approaching four times oversubscribed according to sources familiar with the matter.
cards.body:

cards.headline: General Motors to Develop Energy Storage Batteries as Electric Vehicle Sales Slow
cards.teaser: The automaker will follow Tesla into the grid-scale battery business, making components for utilities and data centers as demand for electric vehicles softens.
cards.body:
General Motors announced plans to manufacture large-scale energy storage batteries for electric utilities, data centers, and other commercial customers. The move follows Tesla's strategy of diversifying beyond automotive applications and comes as electric vehicle sales have not met earlier growth projections. The batteries will help manage fluctuations in power supply and demand on electrical grids.

At a San Francisco event, GM also activated vehicle-to-grid capabilities for its current electric vehicle and home energy customers. This technology allows EVs to help offset the growing electricity demands from artificial intelligence data centers while supporting grid resiliency.

cards.headline: UK Beer Prices Rise 36 Percent Since Last World Cup
cards.teaser: The cost of a pint in the United Kingdom has increased sharply over the past four years, reflecting broader inflationary pressures on the hospitality industry.
cards.body:
Pint prices in the UK have climbed 36 percent since the previous World Cup, marking a significant increase in the cost of one of the country's most popular beverages. The rise reflects multiple pressures facing pubs and bars, including higher costs for ingredients, energy, and labor. The hospitality sector has faced particular challenges in recent years as it absorbed various economic shocks.

The price increase affects millions of consumers who regularly visit pubs and has broader implications for the hospitality industry. Pubs are cultural institutions in the UK, and rising prices could change consumer behavior and affect businesses that operate on thin margins. The beer price surge is part of a wider pattern of cost increases that have hit food and beverage establishments across the country.

cards.headline: Household Bill Debt Increases as Many Remain Unaware of Assistance Programs
cards.teaser: Debt from unpaid household bills is rising while most consumers do not know about special tariffs for water and broadband services, according to a spending watchdog.
cards.body:
A spending watchdog has found that many people paying household bills are unaware of special tariffs available for water and broadband services. These reduced-rate programs exist to help qualifying households, yet most billpayers don't know they can access them.

The gap between available support and public awareness means struggling households may continue overpaying for essential services. Water and broadband assistance programs could provide relief for those facing payment difficulties, but lack of communication about these options leaves many households without the help they need.

cards.headline: Meta partners with Reliance for first AI data center in India
cards.teaser: The social media company signed a deal for a 168-megawatt facility to support its global AI computing operations.
cards.body:
Meta has established its first AI data center in India through a partnership with Reliance. The facility will operate at 168 megawatts of capacity to support Meta's artificial intelligence computing needs on a global scale.

The data center is built with room for expansion as Meta's AI infrastructure demands increase over time. This partnership represents Meta's entry into India's data center market as technology companies expand their infrastructure to handle growing AI workloads.

cards.headline: Apple releases updated Siri with AI capabilities
cards.teaser: Early testing of the redesigned voice assistant shows improved functionality compared to previous versions.
cards.body:
Apple unveiled a redesigned Siri featuring artificial intelligence enhancements at its recent event. The updated assistant demonstrates improved reliability in performing tasks compared to previous versions. The company introduced its third generation of foundation models to support these new AI capabilities.

To strengthen privacy protections, Apple is integrating NVIDIA's confidential computing technology into its Private Cloud Compute infrastructure. Alongside the Siri upgrades, Apple announced new child safety features as the company continues to advance its position in the competitive AI assistant market.

cards.headline: Google cuts pricing for AI subscription service
cards.teaser: The company reduced costs for its budget artificial intelligence subscription tier.
cards.body:
Google lowered the price of its entry-level AI subscription offering. The price reduction makes the budget tier significantly more affordable for users seeking access to Google's artificial intelligence features.

The move positions Google competitively in the growing market for consumer AI subscriptions, where multiple technology companies now offer tiered access to advanced AI capabilities. Subscription services have become a key revenue model as companies monetize their AI investments.

cards.headline: Astronomers identify force killing early galaxies
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered wind patterns that stop massive galaxies from forming new stars.
cards.body:
Scientists found evidence of powerful galactic winds that cause some massive galaxies to stop producing stars. The discovery helps explain why certain large galaxies in the early universe ceased growing despite having the material needed for continued star formation.

The findings suggest galaxies may have a mechanism that effectively shuts down their growth. Researchers observed these galaxy-killing winds in the early universe, providing insight into processes that shaped cosmic evolution. The work addresses a longstanding question about why some massive galaxies stopped forming stars while others continued developing.

cards.headline: Waymo develops new benchmark for robotaxi safety comparisons
cards.teaser: The self-driving car company created a computer model to analyze how humans behave in crash scenarios.
cards.body:
Waymo has created a new computer model to better understand how humans behave in crash scenarios that its robotaxis encounter. The benchmark is designed to enable more meaningful comparisons between how autonomous vehicles and human drivers respond in similar situations.

The tool supports Waymo's safety evaluation efforts by analyzing real crash scenarios the company's fleet experiences on the road.

cards.headline: Nintendo shares fall after game showcase disappoints investors
cards.teaser: The company's stock declined following its presentation of upcoming titles for 2026.
cards.body:
Nintendo's share price dropped after the company held a showcase event revealing games planned for release in 2026. Market reaction indicated investor disappointment with the pipeline of announced titles. The presentation introduced various games from Nintendo and partner studios.

Analysts noted that Nintendo appeared to be taking a conservative approach with its upcoming releases. The stock decline reflected market expectations that had anticipated a stronger lineup of new games for the year ahead.

hero.headline: Hurricanes even Stanley Cup Final with 5-3 win over Golden Knights
hero.body:
Jordan Staal scored twice, including a dramatic game-winning goal while stretched out on his stomach, to lead the Carolina Hurricanes to a 5-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights. The win evens the Stanley Cup Final at two games apiece.

Staal's second goal of the night came while he was sprawled on the ice, putting the Hurricanes ahead for good in what became the decisive moment of the game. The center's performance highlighted a complete team effort from Carolina as they battled back to level the series after falling behind earlier in the championship round.

The Hurricanes displayed resilience throughout the contest, weathering the Golden Knights' attacks and capitalizing on their offensive opportunities. The victory shifts momentum back to Carolina after Vegas had seized control of the series. Both teams now face a best-of-three scenario to determine who will lift the Stanley Cup.

The series has featured tight, competitive hockey with each team trading wins. Staal's veteran presence has been crucial for the Hurricanes, and his two-goal performance continues his strong postseason play. His ability to contribute in high-pressure situations exemplifies the type of leadership Carolina needs as they pursue their first Stanley Cup championship.

The teams will now prepare for Game 5, with the series tied and both franchises four wins away from hoisting the trophy. The Hurricanes have proven they can compete with Vegas at the highest level, setting up what promises to be a hard-fought finish to the championship series.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-1 NBA Finals lead as Wembanyama, Spurs struggle offensively
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks lead the NBA Finals 2-1 after Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs failed to generate consistent offense in Game 2.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks hold a 2-1 series advantage over the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals. Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs offense have struggled to find rhythm against New York's intensity, raising questions about whether San Antonio can mount a comeback.

The series has drawn significant attention from New York fans, with Knicks supporters energized by the team's performance. However, incidents have emerged off the court, with videos showing apparent attacks on Spurs fans in New York following the games. Both teams' players have condemned the attacks as unacceptable.

cards.headline: USWNT defeats Brazil 1-0 in physical match featuring eight red cards
cards.teaser: The United States women's national team earned a 1-0 victory over Brazil in a contentious match that saw eight players receive red cards.
cards.body:
The United States women's national team defeated Brazil 1-0 in a chaotic match in Fortaleza on Tuesday night. Sophia Wilson scored the decisive goal by forcing an own goal in the second half. Brazil finished the match with nine players after receiving eight red cards throughout the contest.

Coach Emma Hayes praised her young squad for their resilience in difficult circumstances. The USWNT maintained their composure and executed their game plan despite the fractious nature of the competition, demonstrating their ability to handle adversity.

cards.headline: Roy Keane and Bruno Fernandes resolve dispute over misquote
cards.teaser: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and pundit Roy Keane have cleared the air after a public disagreement stemming from an inaccurate quote.
cards.body:
Roy Keane and Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes have resolved their dispute following a misquote row. Keane had misattributed statements to Fernandes during punditry, prompting the midfielder to publicly accuse the former United captain of lying.

The two have since cleared the air and settled their differences, moving past the conflict that had briefly strained their relationship.

cards.headline: UFC denies Sean Strickland banned from White House event
cards.teaser: UFC CEO Dana White says no fighters have been barred from attending UFC Freedom 250 at the White House this Sunday.
cards.body:
Dana White, UFC chief executive, has dismissed reports that fighter Sean Strickland was prohibited from attending UFC Freedom 250. The event takes place Sunday at the White House, marking an unprecedented venue for a major mixed martial arts competition.

White stated that no one has been banned from the historic fight card. His comments address speculation that had emerged regarding Strickland's participation in the event.

cards.headline: Scotland coach Steve Clarke optimistic ahead of World Cup opener against Haiti
cards.teaser: Steve Clarke says he feels renewed heading into Scotland's World Cup match against Haiti, sensing fresh optimism around the national team.
cards.body:
Scotland head coach Steve Clarke says he feels like a new man as his team prepares for their World Cup opener against Haiti. The manager is sensing a fresh wave of optimism within the squad ahead of what promises to be a significant match for the national team.

Clarke's positive mindset reflects the mood in the Scottish camp as they approach this seismic World Cup encounter.

cards.headline: NFL teams face key quarterback questions entering offseason
cards.teaser: All 32 NFL teams are evaluating their quarterback situations, from potential extensions for Baker Mayfield and Sam Darnold to the development timeline for rookies.
cards.body:
The NFL offseason has brought quarterback uncertainties across the league. Key decisions loom for several franchises, including whether the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Minnesota Vikings will extend Baker Mayfield and Sam Darnold following their strong seasons.

Other teams face different quarterback challenges. The Carolina Panthers are evaluating whether Bryce Young can improve in his next season, while franchises with rookie quarterbacks must determine the right timing for handing over starting responsibilities. These quarterback decisions will shape each team's direction heading into the new season.

hero.headline: Indian Filmmaker Bharathiraja Dies at 84
hero.body:
Bharathiraja, the Indian filmmaker whose rural dramas reshaped Tamil cinema, died on Wednesday in Chennai from age-related illness. He was 84.

Born Chinnasamy Periyamaya Theva on July 17, 1941, in Allinagaram in what is now Theni district of Tamil Nadu, Bharathiraja worked primarily in India's Tamil-language film industry as a director across nearly five decades. His films brought rural Tamil life to the screen in ways that transformed the industry's approach to regional storytelling.

Bharathiraja's work focused on village settings and rural communities, departing from the urban narratives that dominated Tamil cinema before his arrival. His directorial approach emphasized authentic portrayals of rural Tamil culture, earning him recognition as a pioneer who expanded the scope of regional Indian filmmaking. The director's career spanned multiple decades, during which he established himself as one of Tamil cinema's most significant voices.

The filmmaker's influence extended beyond his own work, as his focus on rural narratives inspired subsequent generations of Tamil directors to explore regional stories with similar depth. His films contributed to a broader shift in Indian regional cinema, demonstrating that stories rooted in specific cultural contexts could achieve both critical recognition and commercial success.

Bharathiraja's death marks the loss of a major figure in Tamil cinema whose work helped define the industry's treatment of rural life. His nearly 50-year career left a body of work that documented and celebrated Tamil rural culture through film, establishing a template that continues to influence filmmakers working in regional Indian cinema today.

cards.headline: BBC Halts Doctor Who Christmas Special, Seeks New Production Partners
cards.teaser: The BBC is not going ahead with a planned Doctor Who Christmas special this year and is seeking new production partners.
cards.body:
The BBC has cancelled this year's Doctor Who Christmas special and will not continue with current showrunner Russell T Davies and producer Bad Wolf. Both have officially exited the series.

The BBC is now seeking new production partners through a competitive bidding process to take the show forward. Doctor Who remains a key part of the broadcaster's programming strategy despite these production changes.

cards.headline: Model Tells BBC She Felt Scared During Alleged Kanye West Incident
cards.teaser: A model who alleges Kanye West choked her during a music video shoot told the BBC she felt suffocated and scared.
cards.body:
The model described her experience during what she said was an encounter on a music video set. West claims the encounter was part of a provocative theatrical performance.

The model spoke to the BBC about the incident, providing her account of what occurred during the video production. West has characterized the interaction differently, framing it as part of the creative process for the music video shoot.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Performs at Toy Story 5 Premiere
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift appeared at the Toy Story 5 premiere, where she performed and released a new track for the film.
cards.body:
Swift released a song titled 'I Knew It, I Knew You' for Toy Story 5, accompanied by a rare childhood video. She turned the premiere into a surprise mini-concert, performing alongside Randy Newman. Swift wore an off-the-shoulder minidress to the event, channeling the character Bo Peep.

The new track marks Swift's contribution to the animated film's soundtrack. Her appearance at the premiere included the unexpected live performance, which featured collaboration with Newman, the composer known for previous Toy Story films.

cards.headline: Netflix Reality Show Desi Bling Draws Large Audience
cards.teaser: Netflix reality series Desi Bling, featuring ultra-wealthy Indian expats in Dubai, has become a hit for the streaming service.
cards.body:
The Netflix reality docusoap Desi Bling has become a breakout hit, following the lavish lives of ultra-wealthy Indian expats in Dubai. The seven-episode first season offers viewers an inside look at an exclusive social circle within the city's Indian expatriate community, showcasing their luxury lifestyle, parties, and personal relationships.

The show's success stems from its appeal to audiences who enjoy watching aspirational content. According to the producer, viewers are drawn to seeing their dreams reflected on screen, which explains the strong reception for this glimpse into Dubai's elite Indian social scene.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Rents U-Haul for Spencer Pratt After L.A. Mayoral Loss
cards.teaser: Jimmy Kimmel rented Spencer Pratt a U-Haul after the reality television personality lost the Los Angeles mayoral race.
cards.body:
During his Tuesday monologue, Jimmy Kimmel joked about holding Spencer Pratt to his promise to leave Los Angeles following his mayoral race defeat. Pratt had suggested he would move out of the city if he didn't win.

The ex-reality TV star's campaign had attracted significant attention with fiery social media posts and AI-generated ads depicting LA in dystopian scenarios. Pratt positioned himself as a solution to the city's problems, resonating with voters frustrated with current leadership. He lost to Nithya Raman, who advanced in the mayoral contest.

cards.headline: Late-Night Hosts Mock Trump Knicks Game Appearance
cards.teaser: Late-night television hosts addressed President Trump's appearance at a Knicks game, joking about the reception he received.
cards.body:
Hosts took aim at Trump's attendance at the game, with one comparing the booing to past incidents at sporting events. One host joked that it was the loudest a president had been booed at a sporting event since Abraham Lincoln flipped the coin at the Cotton Bowl.

The comedians used Trump's appearance at the basketball game as material for their monologues. The reception he received at the arena became a topic across multiple late-night programs.

hero.headline: Republicans demand detailed answers before approving Iran military funding
hero.body:
Republicans in Congress are withholding support for a funding request to finance ongoing military operations in Iran, saying they want clearer information from the Pentagon about the scope, objectives, and total cost of the campaign before backing the measure in an election year.

The military operation, which has now passed its 100-day mark, has cost roughly $29 billion so far. Republican lawmakers are seeking more detailed projections and strategic clarity from defense officials before committing to additional funding. The hesitation reflects concerns about committing taxpayer dollars to an extended military engagement without a clear endpoint or comprehensive plan.

The request for more information comes as the administration seeks congressional approval for continued funding of the operation. Republicans face political pressure in what is described as a difficult election year, with voters likely to scrutinize large-scale military spending abroad. The Pentagon has not yet provided the level of detail lawmakers say they need to justify supporting the request to constituents.

The funding debate arrives at a moment when the administration's Iran strategy faces broader questions. President Trump initially said the operation would last four to five weeks, but it has now extended well beyond that timeframe. The discrepancy between initial projections and the current reality has added to congressional skepticism about committing additional resources without more concrete assurances.

The standoff highlights tension between the executive and legislative branches over war powers and spending authority. Republicans control the House, giving them significant leverage over any funding package. Without their support, the administration may struggle to secure the resources it says are necessary to continue operations at their current pace.

cards.headline: Trump pushes Senate leader Thune on SAVE Act as MAGA base applies pressure
cards.teaser: President Trump's renewed push to oust the Senate parliamentarian and pass voter eligibility legislation is creating tension for the majority leader.
cards.body:
President Trump has intensified efforts to remove the Senate parliamentarian and advance the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act, placing new pressure on Senate Majority Leader John Thune. Thune, who has had an inconsistent relationship with Trump over the years, is becoming a target of criticism from the MAGA base as he navigates the president's demands.

Thune is not up for reelection in the current cycle, but the pressure campaign reflects Trump's willingness to challenge Republican leaders who do not fall in line with his priorities. The push for the SAVE Act and the effort to remove the parliamentarian represent a test of Trump's influence over Senate procedures and leadership.

cards.headline: Iran war passes 100 days as Trump negotiation efforts face setbacks
cards.teaser: The military operation has far exceeded the president's initial timeline of four to five weeks.
cards.body:
President Trump's goal of quickly ending the Iran war has stalled as the conflict surpassed 100 days. Trump initially projected the operation would last four to five weeks, but active fighting continues without resolution.

The extended timeline undermines Trump's reputation as a dealmaker. A recent Iranian attack that downed a U.S. Army Apache helicopter prompted Trump to say the country "must" respond, complicating his earlier optimistic statements about negotiations. Meanwhile, gas prices have surged to $4.16 per gallon nationally—about $1 higher than last year—straining household budgets as the conflict drags on.

cards.headline: House Republicans clash over discharge petitions bypassing leadership
cards.teaser: A growing number of GOP members are joining Democrats to force floor votes, undermining party leaders' control.
cards.body:
House Republicans are expressing frustration with members of their own party who are using discharge petitions to team up with Democrats and force votes on the floor. The tactic, once extremely rare, has been used a record number of times to bypass the wishes of GOP leadership and weaken their control over the House agenda.

Discharge petitions allow a majority of House members to bring legislation to the floor without leadership approval. The increasing use of the mechanism by small groups of Republicans willing to break ranks represents a challenge to party discipline and leadership authority in a closely divided chamber.

cards.headline: Todd Blanche nomination faces Republican anger over anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: The acting attorney general's role in a controversial $1.8 billion fund proposal has created obstacles for his permanent confirmation.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's nomination for the permanent position is set to collide with anger among several key Republicans over his involvement in creating President Trump's proposed $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. Blanche told Congress last week that the administration is not moving forward with the fund.

Blanche is currently serving as acting attorney general while awaiting Senate confirmation. The controversy over the fund, which drew sharp criticism from Republicans concerned about its purpose and cost, has complicated what might otherwise have been a straightforward confirmation process. The nominee's assurance that the proposal has been shelved may not be enough to satisfy all skeptics in his own party.

cards.headline: Bill Gates to testify before Congress on Jeffrey Epstein relationship
cards.teaser: The Microsoft founder will sit for a closed-door interview with the House Oversight Committee.
cards.body:
Bill Gates is scheduled to testify before the House Oversight Committee in a closed-door session regarding his relationship with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The Microsoft co-founder will face questions from lawmakers as part of the committee's investigation into Epstein.

A transcript of the interview is expected to be released at a later date. Gates has previously acknowledged meeting with Epstein multiple times in connection with philanthropic interests.

cards.headline: Trump administration blames Biden for return of livestock parasite
cards.teaser: Officials attribute the reappearance of New World screwworm to immigration policies under the previous administration.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is blaming former President Biden for the spread of New World screwworm, a parasitic fly that threatens the beef and cattle industry. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said the parasite's resurgence is entirely due to what she called lax immigration policies under Biden.

The screwworm had been eliminated in the United States since the 1960s but has now returned. Cases are spreading and pose a threat to livestock operations across the country. The administration's framing of the issue as an immigration problem rather than an agricultural or public health challenge reflects a broader pattern of attributing various problems to the previous administration's border policies.
